chapter: Decca, Cow Cow Blues and royalties
title: Recording with Mayo Williams' portable equipment in 1929 and the Four Quarters
summary: He recalls recording in a furniture store's rug department in Dallas and the 'Sam Price and His Four Quarters' date.

bands.name: Sam Price and His Four Quarters

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I met him in Dallas. But at the time...I met him in '29. I made something with Lem Johnson and...guy played trombone...
Yeah. Nobody said...nobody knows who that guy is. Discographies say, "Name unknown."
Bert something. But I'll get his name for you. I'll give you his name. And I'd had a guy named Percy Darenbourg? playing the guitar. He's a New Orleans guy that I'd met...

Joe Darenbourg? No. Percy and Caffrey Darenbourg, they were cousins. They were two guitar players. But anyway, the guy's name was "berg" something, but I'll give you his name. But Mayo...I was helping him organize the people 'cause what they did, they had like a caravan kind of thing, and they would go into a city
and they would go to a furniture store and go into the rug department...did you know this?...
Yeah, they had recording equipment, and they'd go into the rug department...
The sound, yeah. And they would record in that section. And I recorded this thing with him...something "Four..." what the hell...
